text: I’ll model the fluid domain as a 60 mm diameter, 42 mm long cylinder, split axially into 20 mm flange-bore, 2 mm gasket, and 20 mm flange-bore sections. The bolt holes lie entirely outside the bore (nearest edge radius 63 mm versus bore radius 30 mm), so they do not intersect or alter the water volume. I’ll use explicit cylindrical and planar patch surfaces, then create a coarse conformal 3-D mesh with the three wall sections retained as separate physical patches.

Now I’ll construct the three requested axial sections in metres. Each wall patch is taken from the sole cylindrical face of the corresponding named section, while inlet and outlet disks are constructed explicitly on their known planes; this avoids assigning patches from overall bounding-box positions. I’ll also print the requested dimensions and the bolt-hole clearance from the fluid bore.

The dimensions and volume agree exactly with the specification. I’ll now tessellate the five named surfaces at coarse resolution and render them, coloring the two flange walls, gasket wall, inlet, and outlet separately so the axial segmentation is visible before any mesh is generated.

For a visual geometry check, I’ll also build the two dry flange solids with their six bolt holes. The gasket outside diameter and whether it has bolt perforations do not affect the requested water mesh and were not specified; for context only, I will assume its OD equals the 180 mm flange OD and show it as a simple annular ring. The actual flow geometry still uses only the specified 60 mm inner face.

The coarse view confirms the water cylinder is concentric with the dry flange bores and that the 2 mm gasket wall is separately represented. Before meshing, I’ll export exactly five patch STLs. I’ll use one shared 96-segment circumference for every patch so adjoining STL edges coincide exactly; wall normals point radially out of the water, the inlet normal points in −z, and the outlet normal points in +z.

I’ll mesh by sweeping a coarse triangular disk mesh through the three named axial sections. This gives prismatic cells aligned with the bore, with five layers in each 20 mm flange bore and one layer across the 2 mm gasket. The returned lateral surface from each extrusion is named immediately, preserving the three requested wall patches without positional reclassification.

The coarse Gmsh mesh was generated with all five physical surfaces present. I’ll convert it to OpenFOAM format and run the binding `checkMesh` check now, before doing any further visualization or refinement.

Conversion stopped because an OpenFOAM case requires a minimal `system/controlDict`; no mesh was created or modified. I’ll add only that required case metadata, then repeat conversion in a separate step.
With the required case dictionary present, I’ll now convert the Gmsh mesh and inspect the converter’s patch and cell report.

The converter ran, but that step was not reproducible because `subprocess` came only from the earlier failed cell. I’ll repeat it with its import included. Its report also indicates `defaultFaces`; after making this step reproducible I’ll use `checkMesh` to determine whether those are unintended interface boundaries.

I’ll run `checkMesh` and inspect the patch sizes. If `defaultFaces` is non-empty, the sequential multi-volume sweep has left duplicated internal interfaces and I will replace it rather than accept a disconnected water domain.

The converted boundary contains exactly the five requested patches; `defaultFaces` was not written, so the converter’s “undefined faces” were successfully matched as internal faces. The extended geometry check needs an `fvSchemes` dictionary in this OpenFOAM version, but plain binding `checkMesh` does not; I’ll run the binding check first.

This installation’s `checkMesh` reads `fvSchemes` even for a mesh-only case. I’ll add a minimal standard discretization dictionary solely to enable mesh checking; it does not define fields or boundary conditions and no solver will be run.
I’ll rerun the full topology and geometry check now that its required dictionary exists.
`checkMesh` also requires `fvSolution` in this case layout. I’ll add an empty valid dictionary; again, no solver settings or boundary conditions are being configured.
I’ll repeat the comprehensive mesh check.

The comprehensive check passes: one connected region, 4,994 prism cells, five patches, maximum non-orthogonality 16.5°, maximum skewness 0.212, and positive cell volumes. I’ll now export the mesh to VTK and render a clipped view to verify the axial layering and circular cross-section visually.
I’ll render half of the internal prism mesh together with colored boundary edges. This should expose the five-plus-one axial cell layers and the single thin gasket layer.

The clipped rendering confirms the intended 5 / 1 / 5 axial layers and a continuous circular water region. Before finalizing, I’ll independently weld the five exported STLs and count free and non-manifold edges, verifying that the patch set forms one closed surface despite being split across files.

The STL union is closed and manifold with zero free and non-manifold edges. The finished mesh has one connected water region and all requested patches; no advisory exception is expected.

Measured/requested geometry:
- Bore diameter: 0.060 m / 0.060 m
- Face-to-face length: 0.042 m / 0.042 m
- Axial wall spans: 0.020 m, 0.002 m, 0.020 m
- CAD water volume: \(1.187522\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^3}\), matching the analytic cylinder
- Six 0.014 m holes on 0.140 m PCD have 0.033 m dry clearance from the bore and therefore do not enter the water domain

Mesh:
- 4,994 swept prism cells in one region
- 5 / 1 / 5 axial layers across flange / gasket / flange
- Maximum non-orthogonality 16.49°, maximum skewness 0.212; comprehensive `checkMesh`: **Mesh OK**
- Patches: `inlet`, `outlet`, `flange1_bore_wall`, `gasket_inner_face`, `flange2_bore_wall`
- One STL per patch is in `constant/triSurface`

Chosen assumptions: 4 mm nominal in-plane mesh size; one cell through the 2 mm gasket; the gasket OD shown only in the context rendering was assumed equal to the 180 mm flange OD. That assumed outer gasket geometry is not part of the fluid mesh. All request-critical dimensions and topology were checked.
